solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Glass self-catering house — something unique!

parts.note: SC is the usual abbreviation for self-catering in holiday listings
a oner is a one-off, something without equal

explanation.surface: An advert for a holiday let, glassed in and quite unlike any other.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'something unique' look like a gushing comment, but it supplies ONER, British slang for a one-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall glass for sherry or beer carries this name, as does a sailing ship.

clue.text: Persuades x and y?

definitions.meaning: wheedles or cajoles someone gently into doing something
on a graph x and y are the two reference lines

explanation.surface: A puzzling algebra teacher asks what convinces two unknowns.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it 2,4: CO-AXES, the pair of axes of a graph, labelled x and y; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade someone with gentle wheedling is the verb sense; the graph's paired axes give the punning second sense.

clue.text: Extremely devious lover hasn't finished engaging in search for fetish

indicators.note: one piece engaging in another is set inside it

parts.note: an obi is a charm or fetish, so a hunt for one is an OBI QUEST

indicators.note: the word lover is left without the letters of the next word's synonym

parts.note: finished means over, ended

explanation.surface: A lover breaks off midway through a hunt for some kinky fetish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover hasn't finished' means LOVER without OVER (finished), leaving L, which goes into OBI QUEST. OBI is a West Indian charm or fetish.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblique means indirect or devious, and this is its superlative, so the most devious.

clue.text: One entitled to move below when 23's about

indicators.note: about means going around, so 23's letters surround the rest

parts.note: the answer to 23 down, the two-part word for one who refuses

indicators.note: the letters of below are made to move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone with a title is told to go downstairs when a certain person turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' scrambles the given word into BLEWO; 'below' looks like a direction but is only the fodder. A peeress is entitled in the sense of holding a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress holds a title, so she is entitled in the sense of bearing one.

clue.text: Increase audible output from our star

indicators.note: audible says we want a word that sounds like this rather than one spelt like it

parts.note: the Sun gives out rays of light

explanation.surface: Asking the Sun to turn up its volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to increase it, as with a pay rise or raising prices.

clue.text: Pancake regularly twice tossed into the air?

indicators.note: twice means the letters taken are written out two times
regularly picks every other letter of the word pancake, here the even ones

explanation.surface: A pancake being flipped up into the air, over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures Shrove Tuesday tossing; the definition is really anti-aircraft fire, which is sent up into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-aircraft fire, as an adjective, describes guns firing upward into the sky.

clue.text: Volcanic central part of Canary 20s

indicators.note: volcanic suggests violent eruption, so the letters are thrown into a new order
takes the inner letters of Canary, all but the ends

explanation.surface: A volcano in the middle of one of the Canary Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central part of' takes ANAR from CANARY and 'Volcanic' scrambles it. 20s are islands (20 across); these lie off the west coast of Ireland, not in the Canaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Aran is a group of islands in Galway Bay, so plural islands fits.

clue.text: Other unnamed people impressed by King Henry's executioner

indicators.note: being impressed by something means being pressed inside it

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
etc, et cetera, stands for the rest not named

explanation.surface: Henry VIII's headsman, with a crowd of anonymous bystanders.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Henry VIII, but Jack Ketch served Charles II; King and Henry are just K and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century hangman, whose name became a byword for such officials.

clue.text: (23) is able to do five other answers (according to 24)

parts.note: can means is able to
do as in do time: to serve a sentence
five grid answers (the two-masted schooner, ketch, yawl, brigantine and brig) are all two-masters

explanation.surface: A cross-reference riddle about what one person is able to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: With 23 down in front, the full saying is 'No man can serve two masters', from the Gospel of St Matthew (24 across).
explanation.definitionFit: The saying appears in the Gospel of Matthew, so it is a line spoken according to that evangelist.

clue.text: Cry like a wolf, forever being discovered on return

indicators.note: discovered means its covering, the outer letters, is taken off
on return means the word is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: always means forever

explanation.surface: A wolf crying out endlessly, its howling only found when it comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' turns ALWAYS into SYAWLA, and 'being discovered' takes off its outer letters S and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To yawl is a dialect verb for howling or yowling, the noise a wolf makes.

clue.text: I grin and bear it (smash and grab raid from pirate ship)

indicators.note: smash rearranges the letters and grab takes some away, the raid's letters being removed

parts.note: taken as written: these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A victim stoically puts up with a smash-and-grab raid by a pirate vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters R, A, I, D out of I GRIN AND BEAR IT and shuffle the remaining ten.
explanation.definitionFit: This two-masted vessel was a favourite of pirates, and its name comes from Italian for a brigand's ship.

clue.text: A measure of loss in firkin, maybe, about quart River Bar consumed

indicators.note: in puts the circa-and-quart pair inside what remains of the cask
consumed means eaten away, so those letters disappear

parts.note: a firkin is a small cask, an example of a beer barrel
taken as the word bar
C, short for circa, means about
QU is a shortened form of quart

explanation.surface: A measure of how much ale is lost from a cask, with a quart drunk at the bar by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed' leaves BEEREL once the river and bar letters go; 'in' then sets circa and the quart's opening pair inside. Radioactive decay is the 'loss' measured.
explanation.definitionFit: This SI unit measures radioactivity, the rate at which atoms decay and lose mass.

clue.text: Touching article written about cardinal

indicators.note: the article is written around the other piece

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means concerning or touching on

explanation.surface: A moving newspaper piece written about a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman, but it means a cardinal number, as opposed to an ordinal one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers count things, one, two and so on, and this is one of them.

clue.text: Loud and lewd, I relish Lear's nonsense!

indicators.note: making nonsense of the words scrambles their letters, a nod to Edward Lear's nonsense verse

explanation.surface: A rowdy, bawdy reader confesses to loving Edward Lear's nonsense verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the speaker: 'Loud and lewd, I' am one, and the letters of RELISH LEAR are shuffled to give it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy, debauched person who causes trouble is loud and lewd; the clue's speaker claims the title.

clue.text: Prescription for disease: seaside _______?

definitions.meaning: the instruction that turns the word disease into seaside: sort its letters again
the gap is filled by a holiday town by the sea

explanation.surface: A doctor's advice: for illness, take a trip to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DISEASE, sorted again, make SEASIDE, so the cure for the word is RE-SORT; the same letters fill the gap in 'seaside ___'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside holiday town is a resort, and a re-sort of letters turns one word into another.

clue.text: Hats off to unbelievably impressive flier from Down Under

indicators.note: hats are the tops of the words, so take the first letter of each

explanation.surface: Congratulations to a remarkable Australian pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hats off to' reads as praise, but it takes the first letters of 'to unbelievably impressive'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tui is a New Zealand songbird, so a flier from the Antipodes.

clue.text: Rough veined leaves

indicators.note: roughed up, the letters of veined are disarranged

explanation.surface: A description of coarse leaves with prominent veins.
explanation.definitionFit: This salad plant is eaten for its leaves, a kind of chicory.

clue.text: Bedfordshire town located on the right, round the bend

indicators.note: the right-hand end of the word located gives its last letter

parts.note: round the bend is slang for mad, mentally unstable

explanation.surface: A town found on the right-hand side of the road, just past a curve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' looks like directions, but is slang for crazy. Dunstable is a town in Bedfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunstable is a market town in the south of Bedfordshire, an English county.

clue.text: Road initially tarmacked in secure manner

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word for securing a boat

parts.note: to moor a boat is to secure it

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of tarmacked

parts.note: a way of doing something is a manner

explanation.surface: A road whose surface has been laid with tarmac in a sound way.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorway is a major multi-lane road, the British equivalent of a freeway.

clue.text: Venetian heiress with 12 and a bit acres hiding gold, getting tense

indicators.note: hiding means holding the next pieces concealed inside

parts.note: 12 across is three, and pi is three and a bit (3.14...)
or is the heraldic word for gold
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
A is the abbreviation for acres

explanation.surface: A wealthy Venetian woman with three-odd acres and a hidden hoard of gold, growing anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (3.14..., 'three and a bit') plus A holds OR and T.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Merchant of Venice, Portia is the rich heiress of Belmont whom Bassanio woos.

clue.text: See 26
Foremost of intellects in class

indicators.note: in sets that letter inside the word for a class

parts.note: a genus is a class in biological classification

indicators.note: foremost means the very first, so take the first letter of intellects

explanation.surface: The finest mind in the group stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: an I inside GENUS is the top intellect in a class.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of exceptional intellect stands first among thinkers, a mind in a class of its own.

clue.text: Poet and knight occupying Queen's Square

indicators.note: occupying means taking up a place inside

parts.note: in chess the white queen starts on D1, here written D ONE
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A poet and a knight hold court in a royal London square.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a London address, but 'Queen's Square' is the white queen's starting square in chess, D1, spelt D ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was the great English metaphysical poet of the early 17th century.

clue.text: I don't agree poor Agamemnon's no sport

indicators.note: poor suggests a bad state, so the name's letters are scrambled
no means without, so those letters are left out

parts.note: taken as written, the Greek king, as the pool of letters
a game is a sport

explanation.surface: Someone disputes that the Greek king Agamemnon was a sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Take GAME out of AGAMEMNON and rearrange the five letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man always agrees; the opposite type habitually refuses, saying in effect this phrase.

clue.text: In state of agitation, Henry's going after dull tax collector

indicators.note: in puts the dull-plus-henry piece inside the word for agitation

parts.note: being in a stew means being agitated

indicators.note: going after places the abbreviation for henry behind the word for dull

parts.note: matt means dull, not glossy
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone flustered because Henry is chasing a boring taxman.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew the apostle was a tax collector before Jesus called him.

clue.text: Dope for better luvvie

definitions.meaning: dope means inside information, and a gambler wants ..., the starting price, so the phrase is ...
luvvie is a mocking British term for a gushing actor

explanation.surface: Drugs to make an actor perform better.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it 3,2: THE SP, the starting price, is the dope a better (one who bets) needs. Luvvie is British slang for an affected actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesp, short for thespian, is a jokey word for an actor, the same type luvvie mocks.

clue.text: (23) one without light's one restricted (according to 22)

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: restricted means hemmed in, so the second one is held inside the French word

parts.note: sans is the French for without, also used in English
I again, the Roman numeral one
to light means to land or alight

explanation.surface: A cross-reference riddle about a person cut off from light.
explanation.walkthrough: With 23 down before it, the phrase reads 'No man is an island', John Donne's (22 across) best-known line.
explanation.definitionFit: The line comes from Donne's Devotions, so it is a saying according to that poet.

clue.text: See 8
Resistance infiltrating expansive place of incarceration

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside

parts.note: big means large, expansive
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Resistance fighters break into a sprawling prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a prison cell aboard a warship, and by extension any military lock-up.

clue.text: In the course of candidacy, an insincere colouring?

indicators.note: in the course of means found partway through these words

explanation.surface: An insincere candidate puts a spin on things during an election campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyanin is a blue pigment found in flowers such as cornflowers, so a natural colouring.

clue.text: A work by 22, perhaps capricious

parts.note: per means a, as in fifty pence a pound
22 across is a poet, and his work is verse

explanation.surface: A poem by Donne that could be called whimsical.
explanation.definitionFit: A perverse person is contrary and unpredictable, much like someone wayward or whimsical.
